name: Vista Social
tagline: Schedule and review content across several profiles with a shared calendar

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 15 social profiles, 2 users, 10,000 DM contacts, 1,000 AI credits/month

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 30 social profiles, 4 users, 25,000 DM contacts, 2,000 AI credits/month

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: 70 social profiles, 8 users on the plan card, 100,000 DM contacts, 3,500 AI credits/month
tiers.notes: Annual plan is billed $3,638/year. Another official line says 'invite up to 10 users,' conflicting with the 8-user card cap.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom/unlimited profiles, users, DM contacts and AI credits

pricing.hiddenCosts: X integration costs $29/month on any plan. Listening beyond owned profiles starts at $75/month. Employee Advocacy is free for 3 advocates but starts at $199/month for 25 employees. Scale add-on profiles are sold in blocks of 10 and extra users cost more; exact prices are not public.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Vista Social, schedule and review content across several profiles with a shared calendar. The hard boundary is social inbox, review tools, listening, analytics, and agency collaboration, plus api access, connector upkeep, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Draft and schedule posts for several profiles, preview them accurately, publish through one official API, and retain a shared searchable content calendar.
requirements: developer application for one social network
whatYouLose: social inbox, review tools, listening, analytics, and agency collaboration
moatNotes: API access, connector upkeep, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Vista Social because the scheduler is easy; staying approved and correct across constantly changing social APIs is the subscription. The recurring cost buys OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Active open-source social media scheduling platform.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: Several profiles, a shared calendar, approvals and analytics; the free hosted plan is unusually adult.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: BrightBean's review, reporting and profile-management controls are less mature than Vista Social's established team product.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: Multi-profile scheduling and team review with a shared calendar; deployment is the least social part.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz provides a shared calendar and team features, but approval polish is thinner and deployment remains your job.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

alternatives.name: TryPost
alternatives.desc: Workspaces, roles, comments and a shared calendar across twelve networks; server ownership included.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or production Docker Compose; a bare-metal installation is also documented.
facts.engines: AI writing can use OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the deployment template also exposes Anthropic and Gemini keys.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL or MySQL stores app data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media is local or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: TryPost covers workspaces and comments, but Vista Social's managed review workflow and reporting are more polished.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a SQL database, Redis, media storage, and separate developer credentials for each social platform.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Vista Social Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: There is no forever-free plan, only a fourteen-day trial.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a single-network scheduler DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Vista Social in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one official social-platform API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: draft and schedule posts for several profiles, preview them accurately, publish through one official API, and retain a shared searchable content calendar.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support drafts, scheduled times, queues, campaigns, tags, and a weekly calendar.
Connect exactly one social network using its documented OAuth flow.
Validate character, media, aspect-ratio, and file-size limits before scheduling.
Publish through an idempotent background job with retries and clear failure states.
Store platform post identifiers and refresh publication status without scraping.
Add reusable snippets, local media storage, CSV export, and a token reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out unofficial automation or scraping.
Deliberately leave out multi-network inbox and social listening.
Deliberately leave out agency approvals, white labelling, and enterprise reporting.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
